actions.building: The last build has not finished yet; try again when it is done.
actions.devStageFailed: Building the plugin from source failed. The reason is in the editor log.
actions.k12: Sent to the game; takes effect in about a second
actions.k19: Export did not finish. Open the log to see which step failed.
actions.k8: No usable game profile yet. Create a profile in r2modman and install BepInExPack_GTFO, or click “Choose folder…” at the top right to pick a profile that has it.
actions.k9: “{{v0}}” has no BepInEx. Install BepInExPack_GTFO into this profile in r2modman, or click “Choose folder…” to pick a profile that has it.
actions.pluginMissing: “{{v0}}” has no skin plugin yet. Installing the editor's {{v1}} first, then the skin.
actions.pluginNewer: {{v1}} in “{{v0}}” came from the store and is newer than the one the editor ships, so the editor leaves it as it is; skins install as usual.
actions.pluginUpdate: The game is running and holds the plugin files, so they cannot be replaced now. Close the game; the editor replaces them then. Then click Apply.
actions.pluginWrong: The skin plugin in “{{v0}}” is {{v1}}; the editor ships {{v2}}. Replacing it with the editor's first, then the skin.
app.hotIdle: Game not running: shows at the next launch
app.hotLive: Game running: an apply shows in a few seconds
app.k16: Drop in a humanoid model (.glb / .vrm) to import it; a character project (.forgeskinproj) opens directly
app.updateReady: A new version is downloaded; restart ForgeSkin to use it (the plugin updates too).
character.addSpring: Pick a bone to make it swing
character.applyInfo: Installs this character skin into the test profile to try on. A running game shows it from the next level.
character.applyNotReady: Import a model and match its bones before trying it on in the game.
character.armsEmpty: Nothing is left on the arms: the model has nothing skinned to them, or every material on them is left out in first person. First person keeps the original arms.
character.armsHideInfo: Switch on the materials that should not show in first person, such as a sleeve that would cover the sights. The arms view leaves them out as the game does.
character.armsInfo: The arms and hands you see in first person.
character.armsNeedsBones: Match the bones in the {{step}} step first to see the first-person arms.
character.armsText: The game makes the first-person arms from this model itself: it keeps what is skinned to the upper arms and below (forearms, hands, fingers, sleeves) and puts each joint on the game's own arm, so the hands hold every weapon where the original hands do. You do not make a second model.
character.autoCollidersInfo: Drop the file’s colliders and use the seven capsules placed on the body instead, each switchable and sizable.
character.autoSpringsAdded: Added {{v0}} spring sets. Check each set's kind and thickness.
character.autoSpringsInfo: Adds every loose hair, skirt and ribbon bone as spring sets at once, kinds already chosen — no picking one by one.
character.autoSpringsNone: No loose hair or skirt bones left to add.
character.backwards: The model faces backwards; the game turns it round.
character.bonesInfo: In game the character copies the original moves, so the game needs to know which bone is the hips and which is a hand. Names were matched automatically, and a part it could not find is left empty; click a joint to give it another bone or none. Only the hips must have a bone: the model follows the body by them. Any other part works without one: it does not move on its own in game and goes with the bone above it, so a model without fingers, with one arm or with unlike sides still works. Green has a bone, grey has none, red must be fixed.
character.checkInfo: What export needs. With every line ticked, export the mod from Export in the top bar.
character.collidersFitNone: No body mesh to measure: the shields keep their defaults.
character.collidersFitted: Fitted the shields of {{v0}} joints to the model.
character.collidersInfo: Hair and skirts are pushed off the body instead of passing through it. The colliders are capsules measured from the model's own skin: their shape follows the body and each slice sits on it. The engine pushes a node out of a capsule on every iteration, however deep it went; turn the surface off to fall back to seven rough capsules.
character.creditInfo: The model’s licence asks for credit. Exports put it in the pack’s CREDITS.txt and the mod’s readme.
character.dropHint: No model yet. You can also drop a .glb or .vrm on the window.
character.emptyText: Drop a .glb or .vrm file on the window, or pick one below. The model needs a humanoid skeleton and skinning.
character.expressions: Expressions: {{v0}} morph targets came with the model.
character.fingersInfo: Match each finger from its first joint to the tip. From the first joint without a bone on, that finger stays still; a finger with no bones goes with the hand.
character.fitCollidersInfo: Measures each joint's thickness from the model's own mesh so the blue shields hug the body (hair and clothes are left out). The sliders go back to ×1; fine-tune from there.
character.heightInfo: In game the model is first scaled to the player's height (feet to head, measured on the bones), then by this. 1 is the player's height; 1.1 is a tenth taller.
character.importedVrm: VRM imported: {{v0}} bones, {{v1}} spring sets and {{v2}} colliders filled in from the file.
character.joint.head: Head
character.missingJoint: {{v0}} has no bone yet: the model follows the body by it. Click to pick one; without such a bone, pick the one nearest the middle of the body.
character.modelInfo: Skinned .glb and .vrm models with a humanoid skeleton work (Mixamo, VRoid, Blender exports). Bones, spring bones and colliders a VRM sets are filled in for you.
character.motionGameInfo: The game's own player animations. In the game your character follows the player's body the same way.
character.motionNeedsBones: Match the bones in the {{step}} step first to play moves.
character.motionTryInfo: Extra Mixamo moves, to see how the model holds up in big movements.
character.needModel: Import a model in step 1 first.
character.notSkinned: This model has no skinning, so it cannot be a character. Rig it in Blender and export the .glb again.
character.note.noArms: Both upper arms are not matched, so first person shows the game's own arms.
character.note.noFingers: This model has no separate fingers: in game they do not move, and each hand goes with its wrist.
character.note.noReach: {{v0}}: the upper arm, forearm and hand are not all matched, so in game it does not reach for the gun.
character.note.sides: Left and right look swapped; check before you export.
character.note.someFingers: {{v0}} fingers have no bones: in game those do not move.
character.note.standing: {{v0}}: far from the standing pose, the bone may be wrong.
character.note.still: The parts without a bone ({{v0}}) do not move on their own in game; they go with the bone above them.
character.optionalBone: No bone; it may stay so
character.pickJointHint: Click a joint above to change its bone.
character.pickJointInfo: Click a joint on the figure or a finger square, then choose its bone here.
character.refused.compressed: The model is compressed ({{name}}). Export it without compression.
character.refused.empty: The model has no mesh to show.
character.refused.extension: The model uses an extension that cannot be read: “{{name}}”. Turn it off when exporting.
character.refused.external: The model points to outside files. Export it as a single .glb.
character.refused.image-format: Texture “{{name}}” is not PNG or JPEG.
character.refused.image-too-large: Texture “{{name}}” is too large. Scale it down and export again.
character.refused.mesh-too-large: The mesh is larger than the game can read in one piece (about 2 GB of mesh data).
character.refused.normal-missing: The model has no normals. Export it with normals.
character.refused.not-glb: This is not a .glb or .vrm file.
character.refused.skin-bone-name: Bone “{{name}}” has a repeated or unusable name. Give every bone its own name and export again.
character.refused.skin-bones: Too many bones or broken skin data; up to {{limit}} bones.
character.refused.skin-influences: Some vertices follow more than 4 bones. Limit them to 4 per vertex when exporting.
character.rematchInfo: Drop your picks and match by name again.
character.reopenFailed: Could not open the last character skin: {{v0}}
character.sameBoneNames: Some bones share a name. Give every bone its own name and export again.
character.shaderInfo: Which shader each material uses. Game lighting is the only one for now; it is lit like the game's own gear.
character.shellFitted: Measured the model's surface: {{v0}} points, {{v1}} triangles — and the colliders read off it.
character.shellNone: The picked parts have no mesh to measure a surface on: surface collision is unavailable.
character.shellPartsInfo: The naked body is picked automatically as the collider. To change it, tick materials like picking in Blender, or click a part on the model.
character.shellText: The model's own skinned mesh is the ruler: the naked body (skin, face, neck) is recognised automatically, split by body joint, and each joint's stretch of it measured into capsules — the shape of a leg or a trunk, not a row of cylinders. A pack exports those capsules; the surface stays in the editor as what they are measured from, and as what is drawn. Clothes, hair and eyes are left out by default; tick or untick parts below, or click a part on the model.
character.showBonesInfo: Draw the skeleton over the model.
character.springTooShort: No bones hang below this one, so nothing can swing. Pick one higher up.
character.springsInfo: Make hair, ponytail, skirt or ribbon bones swing. Pick a bone: if several bone strands hang below it (a skirt), each becomes a strand. Use the buttons above to preview.
character.title: Character model
character.titleInfo: Replace your character with an imported humanoid model. Work down the steps on the left: import, bones, hair and skirt, materials, then export.
character.unbindInfo: This part takes no bone: in game it does not move on its own and goes with the bone above it.
character.viewInfo: First-person arms shows only what the game keeps for the arms you see in first person, without the materials left out in step 3. The moves below play on it too.
character.welcome.bones: Match its bones to the game's joints
character.welcome.check: Check it over, then apply it or export it
character.welcome.import: Import a model: drop in a .glb or .vrm
character.welcome.info: Replace your character with your own humanoid model; its hair and skirt swing with physics. It takes four steps:
character.welcome.springs: Mark the hair strands and skirt, set their physics
character.welcome.title: Make a character skin
dance.actionInfo: Import the MMD action file. Conversion runs Blender with mmd_tools and bakes it into the game's format — about a minute for a three-minute dance.
dance.applyHint: Brings ForgeCore, ForgeSkin and the dance plugin along. BepInExPack_GTFO and GTFO_API are yours to install in r2modman first.
dance.cameraInfo: Import the MMD camera VMD, or a .cam that is already converted. In the game the camera follows the player.
dance.cameraNone: Without a camera the game uses its third-person view.
dance.cameraReady: It is converted to .cam on export.
dance.clipHint: Pick a strip on a track below and its settings appear here. Picking a lane's name picks the strip under the playhead.
dance.clipMusicHint: Volume and fades are written into the exported .wav, so this is what the game will play.
dance.clipParamsInfo: Settings of the strip picked on the timeline: trim and slide the strip itself; its own parameters live here.
dance.clipSpeedHint: The action or camera runs at this speed inside the strip; footage past its end holds on the last frame.
dance.deleteBody: Delete “{{v0}}”? The dance and its working folder go to the Recycle Bin, where they can be put back.
dance.deleteFailed: The dance could not be deleted:
dance.emptyModelText: A dance plays on a character: go back to Character, open a work, then come back.
dance.emptyText: Import a VMD action in step 1 and press Convert to dance — it plays here.
dance.exportInfo: Writes the .dance, .cam and .wav files the game reads.
dance.faceInfo: The action VMD's own expressions (blinks, mouth shapes, eye moves) are picked up automatically and written as a .face. A .face file chosen here is used instead.
dance.faceOrMorph: Detected expressions are matched by name to the character's own morphs; a .face picked here is for one baked elsewhere.
dance.frameHint: Camera frame (16:9, only what the camera sees)
dance.morphNone: This action has no animated expressions.
dance.morphOverridden: A face file is chosen: it is used, and the action's expressions are not written.
dance.musicInfo: The song plays with the dance in the game. wav and mp3 both work; it is converted to wav on export.
dance.name: Name
dance.nameInfo: The name is what the game's dance list and the file name show.
dance.noDance: Pick a dance on the left, or make a new one.
dance.noDances: No dances yet — press the button below to make one.
dance.notBaked: Convert an action in step 1 first.
dance.renameHint: Double-click a name to rename it too.
dance.title: Dance
dance.titleInfo: Put an MMD action, a camera move and a song together into a dance the game plays: import the action, cut it to the music, add the camera, then export and install it in step 4.
dataDir.adopted: Now using the ForgeSkin data already in {{v0}}; the old folder was left as it was
dataDir.dev: A development run cannot change its data folder
dataDir.failed: The move did not finish; your data is still in its old place and nothing was lost: {{v0}}
dataDir.info.dev: A development run always uses GTFO_UserData in the checkout.
dataDir.info.installed: Autosaved skins, caches, built packs and logs live here. By default it is Documents\ForgeSkin. Changing it moves all of your data over and deletes the old folder only once the copy is checked.
dataDir.info.portable: Autosaved skins, caches, built packs and logs live here. The portable copy keeps them in GTFO_UserData next to the program by default. Changing it moves all of your data over and deletes the old folder only once the copy is checked.
dataDir.leftover: Data moved, but the old folder could not be fully deleted; you can delete it yourself: {{v0}}
dataDir.nested: The new place cannot be inside the current data folder or contain it; pick another folder
dataDir.notEmpty: This folder already holds other files that are not ForgeSkin data. Pick an empty folder (you can make one in the dialog)
dataDir.same: This is already the data folder
dataDir.title: Data folder
errors.badAtlas: An animated layer sits entirely outside its texture. Drag it back onto the texture on the Layers tab, then apply.
errors.badBackup: The backup of an original file is missing or damaged, so it can’t be restored. Run “Verify integrity of game files” in Steam; it puts the originals back.
errors.badImageFile: This image cannot be read: {{v0}}. Open it in an image viewer to check, or try PNG.
errors.badMaterialTarget: A decal or animated layer sits on an attachment that has no model: delete it, or put it on an attachment with a model, and try again.
errors.damagedGameFile: A game file could not be read; most likely another way of skinning edited it directly. In your Steam library, right-click GTFO → Properties → Installed Files → Verify integrity of game files, then try again.
errors.duplicateMaterial: Two overrides edit the same material: keep one of them and try again.
errors.emptyLayer: Animated layer “{{v0}}” has nothing to draw (no picture, video or text). Give it one or delete the layer, then apply.
errors.fileInUse: Another program has the file open: close it and try again.
errors.gameChanged: The game files changed meanwhile (a game update or a Steam file check). Open “Restore original game assets” to see the state, then try again.
errors.gltfUnsupported: Import a .glb or .vrm model: a .gltf needs its .bin and textures alongside it, which the editor does not take. Export as glTF Binary (.glb) from Blender instead.
errors.k1: GTFO was not found. Click the game status at the top right and choose the game folder.
errors.k10: An attachment has neither a model nor a screen. Import a model, turn on the screen, or delete it.
errors.k11: An attachment is not mounted on any part. Select it and choose a part on the right.
errors.k12: No textures replaced yet. Drop in a texture folder and try again.
errors.k13: The background service stopped and is restarting. Try again in a few seconds.
errors.k14: The background service did not understand this request, probably a version mismatch. Update to the latest version; if that does not help, send the log to the author.
errors.k15: The sound file {{v0}} is not Ogg Vorbis audio the game can play. Choose the file again under Sounds and it will be converted.
errors.k16: A trigger setting is incomplete: “Loop for N seconds” needs more than 0 seconds, and attachment effects need an event and more than 0 seconds.
errors.k17: An image cannot be read. Open it in an image viewer to check, or try PNG.
errors.k18: A position, rotation or scale value is invalid. Reset it on the right and try again.
errors.k19: This weapon no longer exists in this game version. Pick the weapon again.
errors.k2: GTFO is running and the plugin files are in use. Quit the game and try again; updating only the skin does not need that.
errors.k20: This skin has no id. Save the project as a new copy and try again.
errors.k21: This skin pack is broken. Export or apply it again.
errors.k22: Weapon previews are not ready. Wait for the progress at the bottom left to finish.
errors.k23: This folder is not a game profile. Choose an r2modman profile folder (one with BepInEx) or the GTFO game folder.
errors.k24: The ammo screen settings are wrong. Check what the screen shows.
errors.k25: That did not finish. Try again; if it keeps happening, open the log for details.
errors.k3: A file it needs is missing: {{v0}}
errors.k4: Some texture files cannot be found. Check the texture folder, or choose the red textures again on the right.
errors.k5: "{{v0}}" cannot be used as a file name: reserved names (CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, COM1–9, LPT1–9), a trailing dot or space, and the characters \ : * ? " < > | are not allowed. Rename the layer, mesh or sound, or move the file to a normal folder, and try again.
errors.k6: This model file cannot be read. Export it again as .glb or .gltf (from Blender, for example) and import that.
errors.k7: A screen has a size of 0. Check its width and height.
errors.k8: The screen digit font could not be built. Try another font.
errors.noAtlas: An animated layer's frames were not made. Apply again; if that fails, pick that layer's picture or video again on the Layers tab.
errors.noBaseTexture: Animated layer “{{v0}}” is on a part with no texture to draw over. Move the layer to a part that has one, or give this part a texture first.
errors.noLiveryView: The livery is baked in the 3D view: wait until the weapon shows there, then try again.
errors.noPlugin: The editor's own plugin files are missing. Download and install the editor again.
errors.nothingToApply: Nothing in this skin can go into the game files: only textures and material settings (metallic, smoothness, glow, colour) can.
errors.restartEditor: The editor needs a restart for this: close it and open it again.
errors.settingsUnreadable: The editor's settings file (settings.json in its data folder) could not be read: another program has it open or it is damaged. It was left unchanged. Close that program and try again; if the file is damaged, fix it or move it away and restart the editor (then add your own profiles again).
errors.stalePatch: The game files still hold skins written for an older game version. Run “Verify integrity of game files” in Steam, then try again.
errors.unsupportedFile: This kind of file cannot be used. Drop in a humanoid model (.glb / .vrm) or a character project (.forgeskinproj).
errors.workInUse: Another program has this work's files open (an image editor, a folder window, or a virus scan). Close it or wait a few seconds and delete again; nothing was deleted.
exportMod.failed: Could not export the skin mod
exportMod.name: Mod name
exportMod.noIcon: No icon yet; choose an image
gameLog.badAudio: “{{v0}}” did not load: the sound “{{v1}}” is not Ogg Vorbis the game can play, so the whole skin was left out. Pick the file again under Sounds (the editor converts it), then click Apply again.
gameLog.destroyed: The game destroyed the vanilla material of {{v0}} while the skin was shown; the part may not draw until the weapon is re-equipped
gameLog.dropped: “{{v0}}” was installed twice in this profile ({{v1}}); the extra copy is in the Recycle Bin and the editor's copy stays
gameLog.fxSkipped: The code effect “{{v1}}” of “{{v0}}” is not shown: {{v2}}
gameLog.noRenderer: Material “{{v0}}” has no matching part in the game
gameLog.notInstalled: “{{v0}}” kept its own look: the skin it should wear, {{v1}}, is not installed (its pack did not load or was removed)
gameLog.notMultiple: Texture “{{v0}}” is not a multiple of 4 in size, so the game keeps it uncompressed (more video memory)
gameLog.sameId: These skins are installed twice in this profile and the game uses only one copy: {{v0}}. The extra copy is held open by another program and could not go to the Recycle Bin; close that program and pick the profile again to clear it.
gameLog.updateFailed: “{{v0}}” failed to refresh and stays as it was: {{v1}}
help.title: Tutorial
install.load-dependency-failed: {{plugin}} did not load because a mod it needs did not load.
install.load-duplicate: This profile has more than one copy of {{plugin}}, and the game loaded only one. Apply again and the editor keeps a single copy.
install.load-incompatible: {{plugin}} did not load: it can't run alongside {{other}}. Disable one of them in your mod manager.
install.load-missing-dependency: {{plugin}} did not load: {{dependency}} is missing or too old. Update it to {{version}} or newer in your mod manager.
install.load-missing-dependency-any: {{plugin}} did not load: {{dependency}} is missing. Install it in your mod manager.
install.load-refused: {{plugin}} did not load. The reason is in the editor log.
install.plugin-copy-removed: This profile had a second copy of {{package}}. It went to the Recycle Bin, so the game loads only one.
settings.uninstallBody: Uninstall the skin plugin from "{{v0}}"? Gear and characters in game go back to the original look. Installed packs stay in the profile and come back when the plugin is installed again.
skins.deleteBody: Delete "{{v0}}"? The work and its snapshots go to the Recycle Bin, where you can restore them; its copy in the current profile is taken out too.
skins.deleteBodyAdopted: Delete "{{v0}}"? The work and its snapshots go to the Recycle Bin, where you can restore them. It was made from someone else's skin pack in the profile, and that pack stays installed.
store.k1: The background service could not start. Restart the app; if that does not help, send the log to the author.
store.k28: Autosave failed. Press Ctrl+S to save a copy.
store.k4: There is no GTFO in this folder. Choose the folder that has GTFO.exe.
store.profileGone: Test profile {{v0}} is gone (moved or deleted); switched to another available one.
topBar.k21: Plugin removed; weapons in game are back to normal
topBar.pluginPending: Plugin update pending: installs when the game is closed
topBar.testProfileInfo: Apply installs only into this profile, for your own testing; a running game shows it in seconds. To give the skin to others, use Export.
topBar.update.available: Version {{v0}} is out. Click Update when you want it; until then you stay on this version.
topBar.update.dev: A development run does not check for updates; the installed app does
topBar.update.error: Could not check for updates; check the network and try again
topBar.update.failed: The new version did not download; check the network and click Update again
topBar.update.portable: Version {{v0}} is out. For the portable copy, download it from the releases page and unzip it over this folder. Your data folder is not touched
works.addPacksInfo: Install .forgeskin packs someone gave you into this profile, several at once. They do not replace the skins in use.
works.adoptAllInfo: Makes every editable pack here one of your works; the packs stay in the profile.
works.applyInfo: Pack it, put it in the profile and make it this gear's skin in game. A running game shows it in seconds.
works.changedInfo: You changed this work after it went into the profile; the game still has the old one. Apply to replace it.
works.devPlugin: Build the plugin from source and install it
works.installedOnly: “{{v0}}” is in “{{v1}}”; the game still wears the one before, which you can change on the game's skin page
works.lost.compressed: Textures come back from the game's compressed copy, slightly softer.
works.lost.frames: Animated layers come back as their baked frames; the source video, GIF or text is not in the pack. Position and size stay.
works.lost.layers: Some animated layers have no frames in the pack and were left out.
works.lost.meshes: Attachments keep only their game mesh; the source GLB is not in the pack.
works.lost.missing: Some files are missing from the pack; they are marked once the work opens.
works.lost.screens: A screen's font is not in the pack; it shows in the default font.
works.lost.source: Characters come back with the model as the pack converted it; the bone match, springs, colliders, first-person hiding and height can still be changed. The model file it was made from is not in the pack, so the model itself cannot be imported again.
works.lostEditor: Packs keep no editing notes: set the livery and texture sizes again.
works.noCharacterCopy: Characters cannot be copied yet; import the same model again instead.
works.noCharacterWorks: No characters yet. Click + New to import a .vrm or .glb.
works.othersCount: {{v0}} more by others in this profile
works.othersInfo: These skins came from others, were put into the profile by hand or come from other skin mods; the editor has no project for them. You can Apply them, or Move to my works to edit them. A skin mod's belong to the mod manager and cannot be taken out here.
works.pluginUpdate: Skin plugin {{v0}}; the editor ships {{v1}}, update due
works.removed: "{{v0}}" is out of "{{v1}}"; the pack is in the Recycle Bin
works.shippedNone: unknown: its plugin files are missing
